# Stack Research

**Domain:** Dart FFI bindings to a native C SDK (GeniusSDK) inside an existing Flutter wallet
**Researched:** 2026-09-28
**Confidence:** HIGH (verified against the actual header, the actual generated file, and the actual wrapper source — no external ecosystem question here)

## Recommended Stack

### Core Technologies — unchanged, reused as-is

| Technology | Version | Purpose | Why Recommended |
|------------|---------|---------|-----------------|
| `ffigen` | `^20.1.1` (dev dep, `packages/genius_api/pubspec.yaml:15`) | One-time binding generator for new symbols | Already the project's tool; no reason to swap for a hand-rolled parser |
| `dart:ffi` (SDK-bundled) | matches Dart ~3.11 pin | `Struct`, `Array`, `Pointer`, `NativeFunction` for every binding | Already 100% of `genius_api_ffi.dart` |
| `package:ffi` | `2.2.0` (`pubspec.yaml:22`) | `calloc`/`malloc`/`Utf8Pointer` helpers used by every wrapper in `genius_api.dart` | Already imported (`genius_api.dart:12`); covers the new out-param allocation needs with zero new API surface |

**No new Dart package is needed.** Every capability the 12 new bindings require — struct marshaling, `Pointer<Pointer<T>>` out-params, `calloc`/`GeniusSDKFree` — is already exercised by existing code (`GeniusMatrix`/`GeniusArray` in `streamSGNUSTransactions`, `genius_api.dart:827-891`; `calloc<GeniusTokenID>()` in `mintTokens`, `genius_api.dart:488`).

## How the FFI layer is actually maintained (not what the file header claims)

`genius_api_ffi.dart:1-4` says "AUTO GENERATED FILE, DO NOT EDIT... Generated by `package:ffigen`" — but **no `ffigen.yaml` is committed anywhere in the repo** (checked `packages/genius_api/`, repo root, `tool/`). `pubspec.yaml` declares `ffigen` as a dev dependency only; there is no build-runner target or script invoking it. Git history confirms the real workflow: commit `50d7e5d3` message reads *"Regen ffi with load logs. Don't search build linux debug for header file, makes no sense, just pull it from src"* — someone ran `ffigen` ad hoc against a header pulled from the SDK source tree, then committed the output. `.planning/codebase/CONVENTIONS.md:294-298` repeats the "auto-generated, do not edit" claim without ever pointing at a config.

**Implication for this milestone:** there is no reproducible one-command regen. Treat `genius_api_ffi.dart` as **hand-merged, ffigen-styled code**, not a build artifact:

1. Write a throwaway `ffigen.yaml` pointing at the new `GeniusSDK.h` (child functions are the block at header lines 546-720, tagged `/* --- Child Wallet ... (v2.2/v2.3/v2.4) --- */`), run `dart run ffigen` once in a scratch dir to get correctly-shaped output for the 12 new symbols.
2. **Hand-splice only the new symbols** into the existing `genius_api_ffi.dart` (new `NativeFunction` wrapper methods + `late final ...Ptr`/`...Function` pairs, appended after `GeniusSDKGetTaskResult`; new structs appended after `GeniusMnemonicAndInitPath`; new enum value added to `GeniusNodeReturnValue`).
3. Do **not** let a full re-run overwrite the whole file — a blind regen against the new header will reformat/reorder the 27 existing bindings genius_api.dart already depends on line-for-line, turning a 12-function addition into an unreviewable full-file diff. This is the same "smallest diff" discipline AGENTS.md already asks for; it also matches what every prior "Regen ffi" commit in the log actually did (targeted diffs of 30-200 lines, never a full rewrite).

## New structs to bind

| C struct (header) | Dart shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GeniusRegistrationMetadata` (h:91-97) | `final class ... extends ffi.Struct` with `@ffi.Array.multi([128]) external ffi.Array<ffi.Char> game_id;` ×3 (`game_id`, `publisher_id`, `dev_wallet`) + `@ffi.Uint64() external int peers_cut;` | Same `Array.multi` pattern already used for `GeniusMnemonic.mnemonic` (`genius_api_ffi.dart:1128-1131`) and `GeniusAddress.address` (`:934-939`). `dev_wallet` is "opaque bytes/string" per the header comment (h:95) but is still a fixed `char[128]` — bind it as a char array like the others, decode/encode at the `genius_api.dart` wrapper layer only if a caller ever needs it as text. |
| `GeniusRegistrationDiscoveryEntry` (h:102-108) | `final class ... extends ffi.Struct` with `external GeniusAddress child_address;`, `external GeniusAddress main_address;`, `@ffi.Uint64() external int sequence;`, `external GeniusRegistrationMetadata metadata;` | Nested-struct-by-value field, same shape as `GeniusMnemonicAndStatus` already nesting a fixed array (`:1135-1143`). No pointer indirection inside the struct itself. |
| `GeniusNodeReturnValue` enum | Add `GENIUS_NODE_ERROR_REGISTRATION(7)` to the existing Dart enum (`genius_api_ffi.dart:971-993`) and its `fromValue` switch | New header value at h:127-129. `genius_api.dart`'s `_mapNodeReturnValue` (`:1153-1160`) needs no change — it already falls back safely via `try`/`catch` on unmapped ints, but the enum member must exist for a correct (non-fallback) mapping. |

## Out-params: `GeniusRegistrationDiscoveryEntry** out_entries`, `size_t* out_count`

Bind as `ffi.Pointer<ffi.Pointer<GeniusRegistrationDiscoveryEntry>> out_entries, ffi.Pointer<ffi.Uint64> out_count` (ffigen's standard lowering for a C `T**`/`size_t*` out-param — no different from any other pointer-to-pointer). Call-site pattern in `genius_api.dart`, following the existing `calloc<GeniusTokenID>()` / `malloc.free` bracketing already used throughout the file (e.g. `:488-508`, `:900-935`):

```dart
final entriesPtrPtr = calloc<ffi.Pointer<GeniusRegistrationDiscoveryEntry>>();
final countPtr = calloc<ffi.Uint64>();
final rv = _ffiBridgePrebuilt.sgnsLib.GeniusSDKGetRegistrationsForMain(
  mainAddressPtr, entriesPtrPtr, countPtr,
);
if (rv == GeniusNodeReturnValue.GENIUS_NODE_RET_OK.index) {
  final count = countPtr.value;
  final entries = entriesPtrPtr.value; // Pointer<GeniusRegistrationDiscoveryEntry>
  for (var i = 0; i < count; i++) { entries[i]; /* GeniusRegistrationDiscoveryEntry */ }
  if (entries != nullptr) {
    _ffiBridgePrebuilt.sgnsLib.GeniusSDKFree(entries.cast<ffi.Void>()); // whole array, one call
  }
}
calloc.free(entriesPtrPtr);
calloc.free(countPtr);
```

This mirrors the existing `GeniusMatrix`/`GeniusSDKFreeTransactions` free-after-read shape (`:827-891`) closely enough that no new memory-management idiom is introduced.

## `GeniusSDKGetPubSub` is the one exception to "free with `GeniusSDKFree`"

Header h:505-513 is explicit: the returned `void*` handle is **owned by the node**, "must NOT be passed to `GeniusSDKFree()`," and is only valid while the node is alive. Bind it as `ffi.Pointer<ffi.Void> GeniusSDKGetPubSub()` and do not add a free call at any wrapper call site — the one native call in this milestone's 12 that breaks the "everything heap-returned gets `GeniusSDKFree`'d" rule established by every other function here (`GeniusSDKGetInitializationStatus`, `GeniusSDKGetAvailableAccounts`, `GeniusSDKGetMnemonic`, etc. all get freed; this one must not be).

## Isolate question: keep these synchronous, do not copy `selectGeniusAccountAsync`'s isolate wrapper

`selectGeniusAccountAsync` (`genius_api.dart:60-76`, `:993-1007`) is the **only** FFI call in the file that spawns an `Isolate`, and its own doc comment says why: it exists specifically "so the UI thread stays responsive during account switching" — implying account-switch was observed to block the UI. Every other write path that talks to the node — `transferTokens` (`:895-936`), `mintTokens` (`:478-512`), `payDev` (`:1120-1151`), `addAccountWithMnemonic`/`addAccountWithPrivateKey` (`:1039-1062`) — is a plain synchronous FFI call with no isolate. The 11 child-wallet functions are the same shape as those: fire-and-forget submissions (`RegisterChild`, `FundChild`, `RecoverFromChild`, `DetachChild`, `ReplaceMain`, `RevokeChild` — header explicitly calls these "submitted, not confirmed," h:611-612, 649-652, 714-718) or local-CRDT reads (`GetChildBalance`, `GetChildBalanceAll`, `GetRegistrationsForMain`). **Bind them synchronously, matching `transferTokens`/`mintTokens`, not `selectGeniusAccountAsync`.** Wrap one in an isolate later, specifically, only if a phase's app walk actually shows a UI stall — don't pre-emptively add isolate ceremony for 12 functions on a guess (YAGNI; also each isolate spawn re-opens the dylib, `_selectGeniusAccountIsolate:66`, which is not free).

## What NOT to Use

| Avoid | Why | Use Instead |
|-------|-----|-------------|
| A fresh, checked-in `ffigen.yaml` that regenerates the *entire* `genius_api_ffi.dart` from the new header | Reformats/reorders all 27 existing bindings genius_api.dart depends on; turns a 12-symbol addition into a full-file diff no reviewer can check | Scratch config, one-time run, hand-splice only the new symbols (above) |
| `jnigen`, `dart:ffi`'s `NativeCallable`, or any new binding-gen package | Solves a problem this codebase doesn't have — the existing hand-merged ffigen style already covers structs, enums, and pointer out-params | Nothing new; `ffigen` (dev-only, one-off run) + `package:ffi` already in `pubspec.yaml` |
| Wrapping all 11 child functions in `Isolate.spawn` like `selectGeniusAccountAsync` | Speculative complexity for calls with no reported jank; each spawn reopens the dylib | Synchronous FFI, matching `transferTokens`/`mintTokens` |
| Passing the `GeniusSDKGetPubSub()` handle to `GeniusSDKFree` | Header explicitly forbids it — node owns it | Store/return the raw `Pointer<Void>`, free nothing |

## Version Compatibility

| Component | Requirement | Notes |
|-----------|-------------|-------|
| Native GeniusSDK binary (Windows prebuilt, pulled via `CMAKE_ARGUMENTS`) | Built from SuperGenius `c575a16` or later, with `upnp_enabled: false` (per `.planning/PROJECT.md` constraints) | The 12 symbols researched here (`/* --- Child Wallet Interfaces (v2.2) --- */` through `(v2.4)`) do not exist in older prebuilt binaries pulled by the current CMake config; a stale binary makes `_lookup<...>('GeniusSDKRegisterChild')` throw at `NativeLibrary` construction time, not at call time — verify the binary version before writing any Dart against these bindings |
| `ffigen ^20.1.1` | No upgrade needed | Already produces the exact struct/array/pointer shapes used above |
